headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a 0.26% overnight band for a third hour with the low unmoved; Tail holds at 17% while 19-year-high yields keep Stress at 76%
body: The current 00:00Z clock-hour is the third full hour of continuous price discovery since the CME maintenance halt ended, and it again shows the absence of extension. NQ December printed 30,556.00 at 00:15:59Z, down 10.25 points or 0.03%, against an open of 30,560.50. The Globex band reads 30,536.25 to 30,614.00: the session low is exactly where it was at the reopen and the high has moved two points in the last hour, leaving a total range near 80 points, or 0.26%. A second, delayed quote source shows 30,574.75 against a previous close of 30,566.25, on a light volume count, which corroborates the same contained area rather than a competing structure. The pathological path the Tail score describes requires directional efficiency, shallow or failed pullbacks and repeated extension after failed retracements. None of those can be constructed from a market that has now spent three hours inside a quarter-percent range while partially retracing Monday's decline, and the modest drift from 30,594 toward the lower half of that band is itself mean reversion rather than extension. The completed cash session remains the relevant backdrop rather than the current path. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,276.81, down 331.32 points or 1.08%, in a 30,081.06 to 30,480.40 range, with the Dow off about 0.7% and the S&P 500 about 0.8%. Latest-session breadth was broadly negative and unusually concentrated: Arm fell about 8.7%, Qualcomm 7.2%, Intel 5.7%, AMD 3.6% and Micron 2.6%, while Nvidia rose 1.68%; Meta lost 4.8% and Tesla 3.9%. Seven of the eight tracked megacaps closed lower. That is a genuinely difficult tape, and it is the main reason Stress stays at 76% rather than easing with the futures band. The macro anchor is the long end. The ten-year Treasury yield is 5.24%, up about six basis points on the session within a 5.20 to 5.27 range, and reported as the highest level since 2007; the thirty-year near 5.56% is the highest since 2004. Crude added a second day, with WTI at $93.19 and Brent at $105.90, as scepticism about a US-Iran agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz outweighed the restoration of roughly 3.5 million barrels a day through Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline. That combination of higher-for-longer rate pricing, an energy premium and heavy issuance is an environment in which large recoverable drawdowns are plausible, which is exactly what a high Stress reading is for. It is not, by itself, evidence of a path that denies retracement. The VIX supports that distinction: it rose 8.07% on Monday but only to 16.07, within a 15.68 to 16.62 range, which is an unremarkable absolute level of implied equity volatility. Asia is open and mixed rather than one-way, with the Nikkei 225 near -0.39%, the Topix near -1.12%, the Kospi near -0.45% and the ASX 200 up 0.17%. Shared Finviz context was read at the start of this run but its collection timestamp is 20:51:55Z, more than three hours old and therefore stale under the supporting-evidence contract, with its futures and calendar sections marked unavailable. Its latest-session breadth and megacap figures were used only as non-real-time confirmation of the completed cash session and were not allowed to establish anything about current NQ structure. The forward calendar was verified independently: Case-Shiller at 13:00Z, then JOLTS job openings and CB consumer confidence together at 14:00Z, with Goolsbee, Musalem and Williams speaking between 17:00Z and 18:00Z, ahead of core PCE and final Q2 GDP on Wednesday and the September employment report on Friday. The danger window is drawn narrowly around the cash open and the 14:00Z pair rather than across the whole session, because nothing in the current evidence supports a broader protective stance.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the whole of 28 September. The window opened in the Asian session with Tail at 9-12% and Stress near 75%, then moved into the overnight long-end repricing that lifted Tail into the 21-24% watch band from the 03:00Z slot as yields extended and crude firmed. Two hours reached the elevated band and neither persisted: 09:00Z at 26% during the European yield move and 14:00Z at 27% around the US cash open, each back inside the watch band within an hour. Stress climbed from 75% to a peak of 85% at 10:00Z before easing to 76-77% into and beyond the cash close, while Confidence improved from 77% to 88% as the session produced verifiable price-path evidence, settling at 86-87% across the maintenance halt and the Globex reopen. Dominant mode rotated from normal through trend-down during the European and early US hours, to mixed for the second half of the session, and back to normal for the halt and the reopen. Every one of the 24 slots carries a published Claude assessment, so none is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The conditional path begins at 17% for the current 00:00Z hour, where the contained 0.26% band with an unmoved low is the observed evidence, and firms only gradually to 18-19% through the Tokyo hours on an assumption of continued two-way trade near 30,540-30,615. Tail re-enters the watch band at 20% from the 04:00Z Tokyo afternoon, firms to 21-22% across the European pre-open and the London morning, and reaches its highest conditional readings in the US block: 23% for the 13:00Z cash-open window and 24% for the 14:00Z hour, when JOLTS job openings and CB consumer confidence print together and Stress peaks at 83%. It then decays to 20-22% through the US afternoon around the Goolsbee, Musalem and Williams appearances, and returns to 18-19% for the maintenance halt and the following Globex reopen. No forecast hour reaches the elevated band, because under this contract event importance and surprise magnitude raise Stress and lower Confidence before they raise Tail, and an elevated reading would require observed shallow pullbacks, failed retracements or repeated extension that cannot exist in advance. The published danger window is deliberately narrow at 13:30Z to 15:00Z.
